text:
Tia M: hey all, first-day onboarding—trying to build the runtime from source on my Ubuntu 22.04 dev VM. build fails at link with: 
```
/usr/bin/ld: build/runtime_cuda.o: in function `init_cuda_modules':
runtime_cuda.cpp:(.text+0x15a): undefined reference to `__cudaRegisterFatBinary'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
I installed CUDA 12.1 via the distro packages and set CUDA_HOME, ran cmake and ninja. Any quick pointers on what I'm missing?

Jordan: welcome! :wave: short checklist: run `nvidia-smi`, `nvcc --version`, and `ldd` on the failing .so to see which libcuda/libcudart it's picking up. paste outputs if you can.

Tia M: here are the outputs I tried: 
```
$ nvidia-smi
Tue Mar 23 12:05:01 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 520.61.05    Driver Version: 520.61.05    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

$ nvcc --version
Cuda compilation tools, release 12.1, V12.1.105

$ ldd build/libredwood_runtime_cuda.so | grep cuda
	libcuda.so.1 => not found
	libcudart.so.12.1 => /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12.1 (0x00007f...)
```
So libcuda is missing according to ldd; libcudart is present from the toolkit.

Samir: yep that explains it. libcuda (the driver-provided lib) is different from the toolkit's libcudart. if `libcuda.so.1 => not found` you either have drivers not installed correctly or the driver libs aren't on the linker path. quick fixes: 
- run `which nvidia-smi` and ensure the driver is actually installed.
- `sudo ldconfig` after installing drivers.
- check `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/` or `/usr/lib64/` for `libcuda.so.*` and symlink if your distro layout is odd.
Example commands I tell new hires: 
```bash
# set env for cmake/run
export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.1
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CUDA_HOME/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
# if libcuda is installed somewhere unexpected
sudo ln -s /usr/lib/nvidia/libcuda.so.1 /usr/lib/libcuda.so || true
sudo ldconfig
# reconfig & rebuild
rm -rf build && cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=$CUDA_HOME && cmake --build build -j8
```
Also make sure your kernel driver version supports CUDA 12.1.

Natanael: driver/toolkit mismatch is the usual root cause. nvidia-smi showed driver 520 — that's borderline for 12.1 in some distros; prefer >= 525/535 for good measure. If you're on a cloud image that shipped with a vendor driver, sometimes the libcuda ends up under `/usr/lib/nvidia-<ver>/` and not on the default path. If creating a symlink, note that distro package upgrades can clobber it.

eng-infra-bot: If you confirm it's a driver install issue, please file an infra ticket or ping @eng-infra with your machine name and I'll create a temporary support request.

Tia M: ok I ran `sudo find / -name libcuda.so* 2>/dev/null` and found `/usr/lib/nvidia/535/libcuda.so.535.86.10` but nothing at `/usr/lib/libcuda.so`. I updated the driver to 535.86.10 (via package manager) and then: 
```bash
sudo ldconfig
rm -rf build && cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/usr/local/cuda-12.1 && cmake --build build -j8
```
Build completed successfully after that. :tada: Thanks for the pointers — saved me an hour.

Jordan: awesome, great root cause sleuthing. For future new hires I'll add a short runbook to the onboarding doc: `nvidia-smi`, `nvcc --version`, `ldd` on target .so, and check for libcuda.

Samir: +1 — also add note about `CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS` and linker ordering if they run into unresolved symbols during plugin-style builds.

Tia M: will do. who should I ping if driver updates break infra policies? is that `@eng-infra`?

Natanael: yep ping `@eng-infra` and grab a ticket. if it's a laptop/remote dev image, include OS + kernel + output of `uname -a` and `nvidia-smi`.

Tia M: thanks everyone! this is resolved for me now.
